claims.text: An HEA enriched in oxide-forming elements such as Al and Cr will exhibit superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with conventional structural alloys.
The proposed material can be an equiatomic or near-equiatomic Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Al HEA.
A continuous, adherent oxide layer will form on the HEA surface during elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion.
The protective surface layer will primarily consist of Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
The multiple principal elements in the HEA enable formation of a stable dual oxide film.
The dual oxide film resists oxidation under combined wear and corrosion stresses.
The dual oxide film minimizes metal-ion dissolution under combined wear and corrosion stresses.
The proposed HEA will have a significantly lower wear rate than conventional structural alloys under the same conditions.
The proposed HEA will have a significantly lower corrosion current density than conventional structural alloys under the same conditions.
The predicted reductions in wear rate and corrosion current density result from the protective stable oxide layer.
The HEA's advantage may diminish when temperature or mechanical load exceeds the protective oxide layer's stability range.
